The core mathematical structure emerges from the principal-agent framework where moral hazard arises due to unobservability of effort. The model assumes that while performance is observable, effort is not, creating a dualistic dynamic. The fixed-effects approach isolates individual player variation by removing time-invariant traits like innate ability, allowing estimation of the causal impact of contract duration on performance. This is modeled through a linear regression framework where performance declines with more years remaining on the contract, indicating potential shirking. The key insight is that the negative relationship between contract years and performance is not merely due to selection effects but reflects strategic behavior. The breakdown regime occurs when selection bias is ignored, causing spurious positive associations. The telemetry involves statistical validation of the regression coefficients under fixed-effects specifications.
